t:
(a) Texas Star Casino.—
        (1) In general.—Notwithstanding section 12113(a)(4) of title 46, United States Code, the Secretary of the department in which the Coast Guard is operating may issue a certificate of documentation with a fishery endorsement for the Texas Star Casino (IMO number 7722047). 
        (2) Restriction.—Notwithstanding section 12113(b)(1) of title 46, United States Code, a fishery endorsement issued under paragraph (1) is not valid for any fishery for which a fishery management plan has been approved by the Secretary of Commerce pursuant to section 304 of the Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act (16 U.S.C. 1854) before the date of enactment of this Act.  
    (b) Ranger III.—Section 3703a of title 46, United States Code, does not apply to the passenger vessel Ranger III (United States official number 277361), during any period that the vessel is owned and operated by the National Park Service.

fable.w: This section only grants vessel-specific waivers: it authorizes a fishery endorsement for one vessel and exempts another from a statutory requirement while it is owned by the National Park Service. The tempting reading is that the reference to fishery management plans approved by the Secretary of Commerce implies outside consultation, but that is only a cross-reference limiting where the endorsement is valid. Issuing a certificate of documentation is a license-type action, and no outside party is consulted, heard, or given a right to sue.
fable.s: the Secretary of the department in which the Coast Guard is operating may issue a certificate of documentation with a fishery endorsement for the Texas Star Casino (IMO number 7722047)

qwen_block.w: This section grants specific exemptions or authorizations for two vessels (Texas Star Casino and Ranger III) regarding Coast Guard documentation and National Park Service operations. It does not require consultation with, or participation by, any non-federal entities. The only external entity mentioned is the Secretary of Commerce, who is a federal official, so any reference to their prior actions is intra-governmental. There are no public comment periods, advisory boards with outside members, or rights to sue granted in this text.

opus.w: This section lets the Secretary issue a vessel certificate with a fishery endorsement (similar to a license) and exempts a Park Service–owned vessel from a requirement. Neither step requires consulting anyone outside the federal government. The mention of fishery management plans only points to plans already approved in the past to limit the endorsement. It does not set up any comment period, hearing, advisory body, or right to sue for outside parties.
opus.s: a fishery endorsement issued under paragraph (1) is not valid for any fishery for which a fishery management plan has been approved by the Secretary of Commerce pursuant to section 304 of the Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act (16 U.S.C. 1854) before the date of enactment of this Act.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting but wrong reading:** The section mentions fishery management plans approved under the Magnuson-Stevens Act, a process that involves regional councils with non-federal members. But it only refers to plans already approved before the Act took effect, to limit where the endorsement is valid. It creates no new consultation step. The rest of the section lets the federal government issue a certificate of documentation, which is like a license, and exempts a National Park Service–owned vessel from a requirement. Only federal actors are involved.

qwen_chat.w: This section authorizes the Secretary to issue a certificate of documentation (a license/permit) to a specific vessel. The definition explicitly states that 'applications for benefits, grants, contracts, or licenses' are not considered participation. There is no requirement for consultation with outside parties, public hearings, or advisory committees involving non-federal members in the decision-making process described here.
qwen_chat.s: the Secretary of the department in which the Coast Guard is operating may issue a certificate of documentation with a fishery endorsement for the Texas Star Casino
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that issuing a certificate of documentation involves some form of application or interaction with an outside party (the vessel owner), which could be construed as participation. However, the definition explicitly excludes "applications for benefits, grants, contracts, or licenses" from the scope of participation. Furthermore, the text does not describe any process of consultation, public comment, or advisory input from outside entities; it simply grants authority to the Secretary to issue a specific document under specific conditions.
